lammergeier: A lammergeier in flight, a huge vulture with LONG NARROW POINTED WINGS and a distinctive LONG WEDGE-SHAPED DIAMOND TAIL. Unlike other vultures its head is FULLY FEATHERED, cream-coloured, with a BLACK MASK THROUGH THE EYE, a fierce pale red-ringed eye, and a TUFT OF STIFF BLACK BRISTLES HANGING BELOW ITS BILL like a beard. Its head, breast and belly are stained RUSTY ORANGE.
whiterumpedvulture: A white-rumped vulture, a medium vulture with sooty blackish-brown plumage, a BARE DARK WRINKLED HEAD AND LONG BARE NECK, a THICK FLUFFY WHITE RUFF OF DOWN AT THE BASE OF THE NECK like a collar, and the marking that names it: a CLEAN WHITE PATCH ON ITS LOWER BACK just above the tail. Heavy grey hooked bill, broad blunt wings.
alpinechough: An Alpine chough, a glossy JET-BLACK crow-sized bird with a compact body and broad wings, distinguished by TWO BRIGHT COLOURS AGAINST THE BLACK: a SHORT SLIGHTLY DOWNCURVED BILL OF VIVID YELLOW, and SHORT LEGS AND FEET OF BRIGHT CORAL-RED. Its plumage carries a faint blue-green iridescence and its tail is long and square-ended.
wallcreeper: A wallcreeper, a small ash-grey bird with a LONG FINE STRONGLY DOWNCURVED BLACK BILL almost as long as its head, its body held flat and upright with its wings half-spread and its short tail braced downward. Its wings are the point: BROAD AND ROUNDED, MARKED WITH LARGE PANELS OF DEEP CRIMSON-SCARLET across the coverts, edged in black and spotted with two rows of white dots.
himalayanmonal: A Himalayan monal, a stocky pheasant blazing with METALLIC IRIDESCENCE: a shimmering green head, coppery-gold and violet neck, deep blue-green back, and a RUST-ORANGE TAIL. From the top of its head rises a CREST OF ABOUT TWENTY LONG BARE WIRE-LIKE SHAFTS EACH TIPPED WITH A SMALL SPATULA-SHAPED RACKET. Bare turquoise skin around the eye.
barheadedgoose: A bar-headed goose, a pale grey goose with a WHITE HEAD AND A WHITE STRIPE RUNNING DOWN EACH SIDE OF THE NECK, and the marking that names it: TWO NEAT DARK BLACKISH-BROWN HORSESHOE-SHAPED BARS ACROSS THE BACK OF ITS HEAD, one behind the other. Its bill and legs are bright orange-yellow and its body is finely barred pale grey and white.
argali: An argali ram, THE LARGEST WILD SHEEP, a heavy long-legged sheep with a pale sandy-brown body, a WHITE RUMP PATCH and a whitish ruff at the throat. Its horns are the point: ENORMOUSLY THICK AND HEAVY, sweeping out and DOWN IN A FULL CORKSCREW SPIRAL past the jaw and curling forward again, deeply ridged across their whole length.
alpinechamois: An Alpine chamois, a slender goat-antelope with a pale tan-brown body, a CREAM-WHITE FACE MARKED BY A BOLD BLACK STRIPE RUNNING FROM EACH EYE TO THE MUZZLE, and a dark stripe down its back. Its horns are SHORT, SLIM, BLACK AND SET CLOSE TOGETHER, rising straight up before HOOKING SHARPLY BACKWARD AT THE TIPS like a pair of fine hooks.
mountaingoat: A mountain goat, a heavy-shouldered white climber with a THICK SHAGGY PURE WHITE COAT hanging in long shaggy chaps over its legs and a pronounced HUMP OF MUSCLE OVER THE SHOULDERS. Its face is long and narrow with a BEARD OF WHITE HAIR under the chin, and its horns are SHORT, SLENDER, JET BLACK, curving gently backward and unbranched. Black hooves and muzzle.
kiang: A kiang, THE LARGEST WILD ASS, a stocky heavy-headed wild ass with a short upright dark mane along its neck. Its coat is BRIGHT RICH CHESTNUT-RED over the back and flanks, cut off in a SHARP CLEAN LINE against PURE WHITE on the underside, legs and rump, with a dark stripe down the spine and a tufted tail.
tibetanantelope: A Tibetan antelope buck, a slim pale fawn antelope with a white belly, a BLACK FACE MASK and black stripes down the front of its legs. Its nose is SWOLLEN AND BULBOUS ON EACH SIDE, giving the muzzle a puffed look, and its horns are LONG, SLENDER, NEARLY STRAIGHT AND SET VERY UPRIGHT, ringed with deep ridges along the lower two-thirds.
rockhyrax: A rock hyrax, a plump tailless animal about the size of a rabbit that looks like a large guinea pig, with a rounded body, SHORT STURDY LEGS ENDING IN RUBBERY PADDED FEET, small rounded ears, a blunt snout with long black whiskers, and dense coarse grey-brown fur carrying a small PALE PATCH ON THE MIDDLE OF ITS BACK.
alpinesalamander: An Alpine salamander, a slender amphibian ENTIRELY GLOSSY JET-BLACK with no markings at all, its skin smooth, shining and slightly wet-looking. It has a broad blunt rounded head, small black bead eyes, a ROW OF DEEP PARALLEL GROOVES ALONG EACH FLANK, prominent glands behind the eyes, short splayed legs and a rounded tail.
apollobutterfly: An Apollo butterfly with wings spread flat, a large butterfly with CHALKY WHITE SLIGHTLY TRANSLUCENT WINGS, the outer edges thin and almost glassy, scattered with a few solid BLACK SPOTS on the forewings. Each hindwing carries TWO LARGE ROUND EYE-SPOTS OF BRILLIANT SCARLET-RED RINGED WITH BLACK. Its body is furry and grey.
himalayanjumpingspider: A Himalayan jumping spider, a SMALL compact stocky spider with a short square-fronted head bearing FOUR EYES IN A ROW ACROSS THE FACE, the CENTRAL PAIR ENORMOUS, ROUND AND FORWARD-FACING like headlamps. Its body is dark brown-black with pale hair bands, its legs short and thick, the front pair held raised.
woollyflyingsquirrel: A woolly flying squirrel, a VERY LARGE flying squirrel THE SIZE OF A DOMESTIC CAT, its dense woolly grey-brown fur long and soft. A LOOSE FURRED MEMBRANE OF SKIN STRETCHES ALONG EACH FLANK FROM WRIST TO ANKLE, hanging in a slack fold when at rest. Very large dark eyes, small rounded ears, and a long thick heavily furred tail.
